bug_semantics: In aeon.datasets.load_human_activity_segmentation_datasets, pandas.read_csv applies a converter to fourteen CSV columns. For each nonempty cell the vulnerable converter executed np.array(eval(val)); because val is CSV-controlled text and eval retains Python builtins, a crafted expression can invoke arbitrary Python code in the caller's process before the parsed value is wrapped as a NumPy array. The sink is reached both when parsing the downloaded ZIP-backed CSV and when parsing the cached has.csv file.
flaw_origin: The vulnerable mechanism was first written in the original PR #1755 member commit 849946a6862cf8392c1464eb9b8eb63c9007934f, which created aeon/datasets/_tss_data_loaders.py and added the eval-based converter at lines 212-215 (the eval call is line 213). Its direct parent 800c3b5388219850c853d14201a9e841187851f6 has neither that path nor the vulnerable line. GitHub later squash-landed the PR as 8f81a7324a4f116dd862feda68788b03ff9dc39b; that aggregate is not used as the smallest BIC.
ai_marker: absent — the exact BIC commit object names author and committer as Arik Ermshaus <ermshaua@informatik.hu-berlin.de>; its complete message is only “Added time series segmentation benchmark (TSSB) and human activity segmentation data set loaders + tests.”, with no Co-Authored-By, Generated-with, AI, or other trailer, and neither identity is a bot.
evidence: First-party advisory evidence: https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-mp6w-jh5v-fhmr identifies CVE-2026-18286/GHSA-mp6w-jh5v-fhmr, CWE-94, the affected load_human_activity_segmentation_datasets method, and the absence of validation before executing a user-controlled string; it lists affected/patched versions as Unknown and links the fix. ZDI-26-469 independently describes the same method and code-execution impact and names the vendor update: https://www.zerodayinitiative.com/advisories/ZDI-26-469/ .

Fix evidence: https://github.com/aeon-toolkit/aeon/commit/751918052c0cce266b4f7cd4b084408526efc015 (parent ee58d0c290a9360bda414235bfd18b88b728b8b2) changes aeon/datasets/_tss_data_loaders.py from the HAS converter `lambda val: ... np.array(eval(val))` to `_parse_np_array`, which uses `ast.literal_eval` and rejects ValueError/SyntaxError. The advisory and ZDI both point directly to this commit, so fix_sha and direct_fix_sha are the same full SHA.

reasoning: The vulnerability-first trace starts at the advisory-named HAS loader and its eval sink. Source history shows the unsafe converter persisted unchanged from introduction until the advisory-linked fix replaced eval with literal_eval. Main-history -L/-S leads to the PR squash 8f81a7324a4f116dd862feda68788b03ff9dc39b, but reconstructable PR history proves that the smaller causal commit is member 849946a6862cf8392c1464eb9b8eb63c9007934f; the following member only changes a typo and tests. The BIC's immediate parent lacks the entire loader file and the vulnerable line, satisfying direct-parent absence. Tag ancestry places the landed flaw first in v0.10.0, present through v1.4.0, and the direct fix in v1.5.0. Finally, the exact BIC commit object contains only a human author/committer and no AI/bot identity or AI/co-author/generated trailer. Under BIC-only attribution, the closed causal verdict is NOT_AI.
